title: Save immutable print preparations
description: After and only after successful PDF generation, save an immutable `PrintPreparation` containing exact reproducibility and audit fields without asserting that physical printing occurred.
acceptanceCriteria: Each successful generation creates one immutable print preparation with stable identity and timestamp
The record contains the exact project snapshot, output hash, sheet-layout revision and fingerprint, selected positions, uncalibrated status, overrides, and diagnostics
Profile/compatibility and setup-attestation fields are explicitly absent or unavailable when not supplied
The saved preparation can reconstruct the exact canonical renderer inputs apart from separately addressed immutable bundled resources
Existing preparations cannot be edited in place
Failed or cancelled generation creates no print preparation
Preparation persistence failure does not claim complete success or expose a misleading durable audit record

steps.details: Create a versioned immutable record with stable ID, generation timestamp, exact project snapshot, layout reference/fingerprint, positions, output hash algorithm/value, uncalibrated flag, overrides, diagnostics, and unavailable compatibility/setup fields.
Add repository operations to append, get, and list preparations while rejecting replacement of an existing preparation identity.
Construct the preparation from the canonical generation request and successful final-byte hash; retain exact serializable inputs rather than current mutable project references.
Persist the preparation before presenting generation as durably complete; if persistence fails, keep bytes quarantined or clearly label the missing audit and offer retry without duplicate records.
Generate once, reload the preparation, reconstruct canonical inputs and confirm the hash, attempt an overwrite and assert refusal, then verify failed generation adds no record.

technicalNotes: A print preparation is not print history and carries no assertion that paper was printed.
Store user content locally and avoid adding incidental private metadata to the PDF or preparation.
